newsitem.title: PERU: Peru leaves oil privatization program in the air.
newsitem.headline: Peru leaves oil privatization program in the air.

text.p: State oil company Petroperu said Thursday it has not decided when, or if, it will auction the country's second largest refinery, La Talara, despite earlier plans to sell the asset in February.

"For the moment nothing has been decided by COPRI (the government's privatization board) with regard to the continuation of the privatization of Pertroperu's assets," company official Guillermo Seminario said in a written statement to Reuters.

Following concerns that private companies were hiking gasoline prices too high, the government said in December it was studying the possibility of not privatizing the refinery, which has a capacity to produce 62,000 barrels a day of refinined oil.
Talara, which was to be part of Petroperu's piecemeal privatization, is situated in the department of Piura, 655 miles (1050 km) north of Lima.

Within Peru, the series of oil sales has been the most controversial aspect of the government's sweeping privatization program that has also seen sell-offs in the mining, fishing, telecommunications and electricty sectors.

Criticism of the oil privatizations, however, appeared to have died down in June last year when the government sold a 60 percent stake in the country's largest refinery, La Pampilla, for $180.5 million.
But gasoline price hikes since that sale have again focused opposition to the auctions.
As well as the La Pampilla stake, the government has also sold its lubricants unit, Petrolube, and the rights to explore and exploit several oil blocks.
The governmenment had also planned to sell a third smaller refinery, production wells, an oil pipeline and transport facilities.
